title: Rating Rule: CondoGuard Liability Step Charge
content:
**1. The raise.** A liability raise moves the personal liability limit on a CondoGuard Unit-Owners Policy from the lower to the higher of the two personal liability limits the tier offers, which is one step along the tier's liability options, and the declarations then show the higher limit.

**2. Full-year liability step charge.** The full-year liability step charge is the tier's annual premium per liability step for each step raised, rounded half-up to the cent. A raise from the lower to the higher limit is one step.

**3. Charge for the rest of the term.** The liability step charge for the rest of the term is the full-year liability step charge multiplied by the calendar days from the day the raise takes effect to the expiration date and divided by the calendar days in the term (the calendar days from the term's effective date to its expiration date), rounded half-up to the cent. The full-year figure is rounded first and the day fraction is applied to the rounded figure. Each rounding of the liability step charge to the cent is half-up in exact decimal: a figure lying exactly halfway between two cents goes to the higher cent.

## Inputs

| Input | Where it is read |
|---|---|
| the tier's two personal liability limits and its annual premium per liability step | the tier's figures |
| the liability limit now on the declarations | the policy record |
| the term's effective date and expiration date | the policy record |
| the day the raise takes effect | the day the named insured requests it |

## Worked rating (hypothetical figures)

Tier annual premium per liability step 14.00 USD; declarations at the lower limit; a term of 365 days; the raise takes effect with 200 days left to the expiration date.

1. Steps raised: one. Full-year liability step charge: 14.00 multiplied by one, 14.00 USD.
2. Charge for the rest of the term: 14.00 multiplied by 200 and divided by 365 is 7.6712..., which rounds half-up to 7.67 USD.

With the same tier and a raise taking effect with 73 days left in a 365-day term, the charge is 14.00 multiplied by 73 and divided by 365, exactly 2.80 USD.
